models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light SE air and near-flat seas at Filicudi tonight; easy 15 nm motor-sail to Salina tomorrow.
briefing.synopsis: A slack, low-gradient pattern sits over the Aeolians with no organised wind forcing - the models keep the breeze under 8 kt at every island through tomorrow evening, backing between S and SE overnight and swinging E during the day. ECMWF IFS (07 Oct 00Z) and AIFS (07 Oct 06Z) agree on that light-air picture, with ICON-2i (07 Oct 00Z) adding only local sea-breeze variation. The change comes late on 08 Oct into 09 Oct, when the flow shifts into the SW then NW behind a trough and gust fields jump sharply - IFS shows gusts to 30.3 kt at Lipari at midnight 09 Oct and 42.8 kt at Stromboli at midday, against mean winds under 10 kt.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Filicudi Porto is the recommendation and is scored sheltered (0.899), with 5 kt ESE, gusts 11 kt and 0.7 ft E swell - Pecorini a Mare scores effectively the same (0.892), so the choice does not matter tonight. Filicudi Porto is open through 345-099 deg, so the ESE is on the edge of that sector, but at 5 kt it is nothing. Filicudi sits at 6.9 kt E with 0.9 ft wave at 18:00 and eases to 3.8 kt by midnight (IFS, 07 Oct 00Z). Only a genuine build in the E would be a reason to shift round to Pecorini.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Filicudi is forecast at 2.2 kt S with 0.5 ft wave at 06:00, so the recommended departure of 06:00 is a motor-out in glass. The whole day is rated go: 3.4 kt S beam reach at 06:00 building only to 5.5 kt E by the 14:00 window, waves 0.4-0.5 ft throughout. The window is effectively open all day - leaving by mid-morning keeps you sailing on a close reach before the breeze goes head-on and the 15 nm becomes an engine job.

passage_notes.note: 15 nm, 092 deg T. All five windows go. Best sailing angle is 06:00-10:00 (S to SSE, 3-5 kt, TWA 82 down to 63); by midday the wind is ESE to E and you are head to wind - motor. Waves 0.4-0.5 ft. Gusts of 11-16 kt against 3-6 kt means are IFS interval maxima in light air, not squalls.

24 nm, 156 deg T, recommended departure 07:00 with conditions flagged as deteriorating after 08:00. The 06:00 window is no-go on forecast thunderstorms and the 08:00 window is no-go on gusts of 32.3 kt. Later windows compute as go on 8-10 kt means from the NNW/N, but gusts run 25.9-36.3 kt and wave builds from 1.0 to 1.6 ft. Treat this as a day to re-brief, not to plan firmly tonight.

cautions: 09 Oct is the day to watch: thunderstorms in the 06:00-10:00 window out of Salina, and gust figures of 26-36 kt on the passage, 38.7 kt at Panarea and 42.8 kt at Stromboli at midday (IFS, 07 Oct 00Z). The computed go verdicts on the later windows rest on light mean winds and do not account for those gusts well - skipper's call.
Models disagree materially on 09 Oct wind speed: Panarea midday spans 3.2-15.6 kt, Stromboli 2.7-14.0 kt, Salina 3.3-12.9 kt. That is a spread, not a forecast - do not plan to a single number.
Gust-to-mean ratios all week are large because the IFS gust field is an interval maximum in light air. Useful as a ceiling, misleading as an expectation.
briefing.confidence_note: IFS, AIFS and ICON-2i agree closely on tonight and tomorrow - stability tracking shows mean wind shifts of only 1.0-1.1 kt at 12-48 h lead - but the models diverge by more than 6 kt at several points on 09 Oct, which pulls the overall call down.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
